Definition: from a prolonged compound of the base of G2360; and a derivative of G680 (meaning a noisy iambus, sung in honor of Bacchus); to make an acclamatory procession, i.e. (figuratively) to conquer or (by Hebraism) to give victory:--(cause) to triumph (over).
BiblicalUsage: thriambeúō is the Bible's word for to triumph. In 2 Corinthians 2:14, which always causeth us to triumph in Christ, and it appears again in Colossians 2:15.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that Christ’s triumph is not a future hope only; it is the ground I stand on now.
